questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What quarter-comma meantone compromises
questions.stem: Translator note 1 asks what quarter-comma meantone compromises to sweeten major thirds.

options.text: It compromises the purity of five fifths, narrowing each by a quarter comma.
It compromises rhythm, slowing all tempos.
It compromises dynamics, softening all chords.

questions.explanation: Quarter-comma meantone narrows five fifths by a quarter comma each to make major thirds pure. The cost falls on those five fifths.

questions.topic: The size of a quarter-comma meantone fifth
questions.stem: Translator note 2 computes a quarter-comma meantone fifth: 702 cents minus one quarter of a syntonic comma (about 5.4 cents).
questions.explanation: A pure fifth of 702 cents minus one quarter of a syntonic comma (about 5.4 cents) gives roughly 696.6 cents. This is the meantone fifth.

answer.exemplar: In quarter-comma meantone the major third is pure, measuring about 386 cents, the just 5:4 ratio.

questions.explanation: Quarter-comma meantone makes major thirds pure at about 386 cents. That purity is the whole point of the temperament.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The two semitone sizes in quarter-comma meantone
questions.stem: Translator note 4 asks which two semitone sizes occur in quarter-comma meantone.

options.text: A chromatic and a diatonic semitone of different sizes.
Two equal semitones of 100 cents each.

A major and a minor semitone of identical size.

questions.explanation: Quarter-comma meantone has two distinct semitone sizes: a larger diatonic semitone and a smaller chromatic one. Equal temperament is the one with equal semitones.

answer.exemplar: The quarter-comma meantone major third is pure, measuring about 386 cents, the just 5:4 ratio.

questions.explanation: About 386 cents, the pure 5:4 major third. That purity is the temperament's goal.

questions.topic: Transposing a note by a number of semitones
questions.stem: Translator note 60 asks what note results from transposing C up by 7 semitones.

answer.exemplar: Transposing C up by seven semitones yields G, a perfect fifth above the starting note.

questions.explanation: Seven semitones above C is G, a perfect fifth. The transposition distance is seven.
